description: This topic explains the chemistry of air, water and land pollution, the sources and effects of common pollutants such as carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and CFCs, and the chemical methods used to control and treat pollution for a cleaner environment in Tanzania and Africa.

mcq.questionText: From a chemical viewpoint, a pollutant is best described as a substance that:

options.text: is always a naturally occurring gas in clean air
is added to the environment in harmful amounts and causes damage to living things or materials
is only found inside chemistry laboratories
improves the quality of air, water and soil

mcq.explanation: Pollution is the addition of harmful substances (pollutants) to the environment in amounts that damage living organisms, materials or natural balance.

mcq.questionText: Carbon monoxide (CO) is dangerous to humans mainly because it:

options.text: dissolves in rain to form an acid
combines with haemoglobin and reduces oxygen transport in the blood
makes water turn green with algae

mcq.explanation: CO binds strongly to haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin, preventing the blood from carrying enough oxygen, which can cause death.

mcq.questionText: Which gas is the main cause of the greenhouse effect and global warming?
mcq.explanation: Carbon dioxide traps heat radiated from the Earth, increasing global temperatures (the greenhouse effect).

mcq.questionText: Acid rain is caused mainly by the release of sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen, which in the atmosphere form:
mcq.explanation: SO2 forms sulphuric acid and oxides of nitrogen form nitric acid when they dissolve in atmospheric water, producing acid rain.

mcq.questionText: The depletion of the ozone layer in the upper atmosphere is mainly caused by:
mcq.explanation: CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere that catalytically destroy ozone (O3) molecules.

mcq.questionText: A major source of sulphur dioxide pollution is:

options.text: burning of fossil fuels that contain sulphur impurities

mcq.explanation: Coal and oil contain sulphur impurities; when burnt in power stations and industries they release SO2.

mcq.questionText: Eutrophication of water bodies such as parts of Lake Victoria is caused mainly by:

options.text: excess nitrate and phosphate fertilisers washed into the water
too much carbon dioxide in the air

mcq.explanation: Nitrates and phosphates from fertilisers cause rapid growth of algae; when the algae decay, oxygen is used up and aquatic life dies.

mcq.questionText: A catalytic converter fitted to a car exhaust helps to reduce pollution by converting:

options.text: carbon monoxide and oxides of nitrogen into carbon dioxide and nitrogen

mcq.explanation: Catalytic converters use metals such as platinum to convert harmful CO and NOx into less harmful CO2 and N2.

mcq.questionText: Which heavy metal, formerly added to petrol, is a serious pollutant that damages the brain and nervous system?
mcq.explanation: Lead compounds were once added to petrol as anti-knock agents; lead is toxic and harms the nervous system, so unleaded fuel is now used.

mcq.questionText: Particulates (smoke and soot) in the air are best described as:

options.text: tiny solid particles suspended in the air

mcq.explanation: Particulates are fine solid particles such as soot from incomplete combustion; they cause respiratory diseases and reduce visibility.

mcq.questionText: Untreated sewage discharged into rivers causes water pollution mainly because it:

options.text: carries disease-causing organisms and uses up dissolved oxygen during decay

mcq.explanation: Sewage contains pathogens and organic matter; bacteria decomposing the organic matter consume dissolved oxygen, killing fish and spreading disease such as cholera.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a chemical method of reducing sulphur dioxide emissions from a factory chimney?

options.text: Fitting scrubbers that pass the gases through an alkaline (basic) solution
Increasing the amount of coal burnt
Cooling the gases with water vapour

mcq.explanation: Scrubbers pass waste gases through an alkali such as calcium hydroxide or calcium oxide, which neutralises and removes acidic SO2.

mcq.questionText: The greenhouse effect would increase most if there was a large rise in the amount of which gas from burning fossil fuels and deforestation?
mcq.explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases CO2 while cutting forests reduces its absorption, raising CO2 levels and intensifying the greenhouse effect.

mcq.questionText: Recycling materials such as plastics, glass and metals helps to control pollution mainly because it:

options.text: increases the amount of waste in landfills
reduces waste and saves raw materials and energy

mcq.explanation: Recycling reduces the volume of solid waste, conserves raw materials, and uses less energy than making new products, lowering pollution.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best explains why plastics are a serious land pollution problem?

options.text: They dissolve easily in rain water
They are non-biodegradable and remain in the soil for a very long time
They quickly turn into fertile soil
They are eaten by all soil bacteria

mcq.explanation: Most plastics are non-biodegradable, so they accumulate in soil and water; this is why Tanzania banned single-use plastic bags.

fib.questionText: The addition of harmful substances to the environment in amounts that damage living things is called _____.
fib.explanation: Pollution is the introduction of harmful substances (pollutants) into the environment.

fib.questionText: The gas that combines with haemoglobin in the blood and reduces oxygen transport is _____.
fib.explanation: Carbon monoxide (CO) forms carboxyhaemoglobin, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.

fib.questionText: Sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen dissolve in atmospheric water to produce _____ rain.
fib.explanation: These acidic gases form sulphuric and nitric acids, giving acid rain that damages buildings, soil and aquatic life.

fib.questionText: The layer of gas in the upper atmosphere that protects living things from harmful ultraviolet radiation is the _____ layer.
fib.explanation: The ozone (O3) layer absorbs harmful UV radiation; it is depleted by CFCs.

fib.questionText: The compounds, once used in refrigerators and aerosol sprays, that destroy the ozone layer are called _____.
fib.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) release chlorine atoms that break down ozone molecules.

fib.questionText: The over-enrichment of water by nitrates and phosphates, leading to excessive algal growth, is called _____.
fib.explanation: Eutrophication results from fertiliser run-off, causing algal blooms that use up oxygen when they decay.

fib.questionText: A device fitted in a car exhaust to convert carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides into less harmful gases is a catalytic _____.
fib.explanation: A catalytic converter uses metal catalysts to change CO and NOx into CO2 and N2.

fib.questionText: The toxic heavy metal that was formerly added to petrol as an anti-knock agent is _____.
fib.explanation: Lead compounds were added to petrol; because lead is poisonous, unleaded fuel is now used.

fib.questionText: Fine solid particles such as soot and dust suspended in the air are known as _____.
fib.explanation: Particulates come mainly from incomplete combustion and cause respiratory diseases.

fib.questionText: The branch of chemistry that designs products and processes to reduce or prevent pollution is called _____ chemistry.
fib.explanation: Green chemistry aims to prevent waste, use safer chemicals and conserve energy to protect the environment.

tf.questionText: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming.
tf.explanation: Carbon dioxide traps heat radiated by the Earth and is the main greenhouse gas.

tf.questionText: Carbon monoxide is produced by the complete combustion of carbon fuels in plenty of oxygen.
tf.explanation: Carbon monoxide is produced by incomplete combustion in a limited supply of oxygen; complete combustion gives carbon dioxide.

tf.questionText: Acid rain can damage buildings made of limestone and marble.
tf.explanation: Acid rain reacts with calcium carbonate in limestone and marble, slowly dissolving and corroding the stone.

tf.questionText: CFCs are harmless to the ozone layer.
tf.explanation: CFCs release chlorine atoms that destroy ozone, causing ozone depletion.

tf.questionText: Discharging untreated industrial effluent containing heavy metals into rivers can poison fish and people who use the water.
tf.explanation: Heavy metals such as mercury and lead are toxic and accumulate in living tissue, harming aquatic life and humans.

tf.questionText: Eutrophication increases the amount of dissolved oxygen available for fish in a lake.
tf.explanation: Eutrophication decreases dissolved oxygen because decaying algae use up oxygen, killing fish.

tf.questionText: Using unleaded petrol helps to reduce the amount of toxic lead released into the air.
tf.explanation: Unleaded petrol contains no lead anti-knock additives, so it does not release toxic lead compounds.

tf.questionText: Most plastics are biodegradable and decay quickly in the soil.
tf.explanation: Most plastics are non-biodegradable and persist in the environment for many years, causing land and water pollution.

tf.questionText: Scrubbers can remove acidic gases such as sulphur dioxide from factory chimneys by passing them through an alkaline solution.
tf.explanation: Alkaline scrubbers neutralise acidic SO2, removing it before the gases leave the chimney.

tf.questionText: Laws such as the ban on plastic bags in Tanzania and the action of individuals both help to control pollution.
tf.explanation: Government laws and responsible individual behaviour, such as proper waste disposal and recycling, both reduce pollution.

summary.questionText: Define pollution and a pollutant from a chemical point of view.
summary.correctAnswer: Pollution is the addition of harmful substances to the air, water or land in amounts that damage living things, materials or the natural balance of the environment. A pollutant is the harmful substance itself, for example carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide or plastic waste.
summary.explanation: These definitions form the foundation of environmental chemistry.

summary.questionText: List four common air pollutants and one source of each.
summary.correctAnswer: Carbon monoxide from incomplete combustion in car engines; sulphur dioxide from burning sulphur-containing fossil fuels; nitrogen oxides from vehicle and industrial combustion; and particulates (soot) from burning fuels and bush fires.
summary.explanation: Knowing pollutants and their sources is key to controlling air pollution.

summary.questionText: Explain how acid rain is formed and state two of its harmful effects.
summary.correctAnswer: When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen are released. In the atmosphere these gases dissolve in water vapour to form sulphuric acid and nitric acid, which fall as acid rain. Acid rain corrodes buildings and metals and makes soil and lakes too acidic for plants and aquatic life.
summary.explanation: Acid rain shows how acidic oxides cause chemical damage to the environment.

summary.questionText: Describe the greenhouse effect and how it leads to global warming.
summary.correctAnswer: Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide allow sunlight to reach the Earth but trap the heat radiated back from the surface. This trapped heat raises the average temperature of the atmosphere, a process called global warming, which causes climate change, melting ice and rising sea levels.
summary.explanation: The greenhouse effect links rising CO2 to global warming and climate change.

summary.questionText: Explain how CFCs cause depletion of the ozone layer and why this is harmful.
summary.correctAnswer: CFCs rise into the upper atmosphere where ultraviolet light breaks them down to release chlorine atoms. Each chlorine atom catalytically destroys many ozone molecules, thinning the ozone layer. This allows more harmful ultraviolet radiation to reach the Earth, increasing skin cancer and damaging crops.
summary.explanation: Ozone depletion is an example of a catalytic chemical reaction with serious effects.

summary.questionText: State four sources of water pollution.
summary.correctAnswer: Sources of water pollution include untreated sewage, industrial effluent, fertilisers (nitrates and phosphates) causing eutrophication, oil spills, and heavy metals such as mercury and lead.
summary.explanation: Water pollution comes from domestic, agricultural and industrial sources.

summary.questionText: Explain how a catalytic converter reduces air pollution from cars.
summary.correctAnswer: A catalytic converter contains metal catalysts such as platinum and rhodium. As exhaust gases pass over it, carbon monoxide and oxides of nitrogen are converted into less harmful carbon dioxide and nitrogen gas, reducing the amount of toxic gases released into the air.
summary.explanation: Catalytic converters are a chemical control method for vehicle emissions.

summary.questionText: Describe three chemical or practical methods of controlling and treating pollution.
summary.correctAnswer: Pollution can be controlled by fitting scrubbers to neutralise acidic gases, using catalytic converters on vehicles, treating sewage and water before release, using unleaded fuel, and recycling waste materials such as plastics and metals.
summary.explanation: A combination of chemical treatment and good practice reduces pollution.

summary.questionText: State three principles of green chemistry.
summary.correctAnswer: Green chemistry principles include preventing waste rather than treating it, using safer and less toxic chemicals, conserving energy, using renewable raw materials, and designing products that break down safely after use.
summary.explanation: Green chemistry aims to prevent pollution at the design stage.

summary.questionText: Explain the role of laws and of individuals in controlling pollution, using a Tanzanian example.
summary.correctAnswer: Laws set rules and penalties that force factories and people to control pollution, for example Tanzania's ban on plastic carrier bags and rules on industrial waste disposal. Individuals help by disposing of waste properly, recycling, planting trees and avoiding burning rubbish, so that both government and citizens protect the environment together.
summary.explanation: Pollution control needs both legal enforcement and responsible individual action.

hoq.questionText: A factory in Mwanza burns coal containing sulphur and releases the gases through a chimney. Villagers nearby report that their iron roofs corrode quickly and crops grow poorly. Which explanation best fits these observations?

options.text: Carbon dioxide from the chimney is fertilising the crops too much
Sulphur dioxide forms acid rain that corrodes the iron roofs and makes the soil too acidic for crops
Ozone from the chimney is protecting the roofs
Nitrogen gas from the chimney is poisoning the soil

hoq.explanation: Burning sulphur-rich coal produces SO2, which forms sulphuric acid in rain; acid rain corrodes metals and lowers soil pH, harming crops.

hoq.questionText: A town empties large amounts of fertiliser run-off and sewage into a calm bay of Lake Victoria. Over time the water turns green, then fish are found dead. Which sequence correctly explains what happened?

options.text: Nutrients caused algae to grow rapidly; when the algae died, bacteria decomposing them used up the dissolved oxygen, so the fish suffocated
The fertilisers added extra oxygen, which poisoned the fish
The sewage cooled the water until the fish froze
Carbon dioxide from the air dissolved and turned the water green

hoq.explanation: This is eutrophication: nitrates and phosphates trigger algal blooms; decay of the algae consumes dissolved oxygen, killing fish.

hoq.questionText: An engineer wants to design a city bus fleet that produces the least harmful exhaust pollution. Which combination of measures is chemically the most effective?

options.text: Use leaded petrol and remove the catalytic converters
Burn more fuel per kilometre and use a taller exhaust pipe only
Use unleaded fuel with catalytic converters so carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides are converted to carbon dioxide and nitrogen
Add sulphur to the fuel to make it burn hotter

hoq.explanation: Unleaded fuel avoids toxic lead emissions, and catalytic converters change CO and NOx into less harmful CO2 and N2, giving the cleanest exhaust.
